races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old front-runner in excellent recent form with three wins from his last five starts, all at 1m-1m2f on good ground; Tim Easterby's yard is firing at T14 6/79, Jake Dickson (5lb claimer) reduces weight, and his single soft-ground run yielded no win or place but today's sole-leader role and uncontested pace are significant positives.
runners_data.comment: Poet's Dawn arrives on the back of three wins in his last six starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that his last two runs have yielded a seventh and a ninth, raising questions about current form.

runners_data.name: Triple Force
runners_data.note: Prominent-style five-year-old returning after a 66-day break which is a mild concern, but Craig Lidster sends him here with three placings in his last five and a consistent record at 1m2f on good ground; no soft-ground wins in the sample and the layoff means freshness could cut either way.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a place finish on soft and solid placed form at this trip for Tina Jackson; Warren Fentiman takes over in the saddle and the horse arrives 17 days fresh — six runs showing two seconds and a third suggest reliability without dominance.
runners_data.comment: Placed in four of his last five starts, His Finest Hour arrives here fresh after 17 days, has run over today's trip, and carries 138 lb from stall three; winless in recent starts but his strong profile of seconds and thirds marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who will try to come from off the pace, though two recent second-place finishes at 1m2f on good suggest he handles the trip well; soft-ground form is mixed across seven runs and Rhys Elliott's 3lb claim helps, but this style depends on the pace being truly strong enough to set up a late run.
runners_data.comment: Yermanthere showed his worth with back-to-back seconds and a win earlier in this run of form, giving him solid recent form, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is that sixth last time out suggests he can find one or two too good.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fitted with tongue-plus headgear, arriving 20 days since his last run with a modest form string that includes just one place in his last five; James Owen's yard is running at 2/40 in the past 14 days and there is little in the record to inspire confidence on soft ground at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back offers a crumb of comfort for No Knee Never, but he arrives winless in his last six starts and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past fortnight is a concern, even if experience over today's trip and going keeps him in the conversation from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: Prominent-style four-year-old with a win and two places in 13 soft-ground runs — the best soft-ground credentials among the prominent group; Shay Farmer's 3lb claim is useful and Michael & David Easterby send him out after 24 days, but a string of finishes outside the top three recently tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Draupnir has run over today's trip and going and, with our rating putting him second of seven in this field, he arrives with genuine claims as a leading threat; the worry is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and his recent finishing positions make improvement the key ask.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Useful form profile including a win and a place in 15 soft-ground starts, and David O'Meara's record of 3/40 over 14 days suggests reasonable stable form; however, this horse's natural inclination is to race from the back and being pushed into a midfield slot in a field heavy with hold-up types means it is unlikely to secure its optimal position — factor that into any assessment of its chance.
runners_data.comment: Cosmos Raj returns on a quick ten-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures he faces a stiff task, and four consecutive finishes off the frame in his last six starts before that recent win make him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Precious Spartan
runners_data.note: A four-year-old whose recent form reads poorly — nothing better than ninth from eight furlongs to ten furlongs — and Patrick Neville's yard has gone 0/5 in the past 14 days; shares soft-ground placed form at 7f-8f but is operating out of its most natural patient style today, slotted into midfield rather than the deep rear it would prefer, which further constrains its already modest winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an unplaced effort latest and finishes of eighth and ninth in the two runs prior, Precious Spartan faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures; a third four starts back and distance-and-going experience at least offer slim crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Poet's Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 1m2f Soft-ground Ripon handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival likely to pressure him from the outset, giving Jake Dickson every chance to dictate a controlled, measured gallop off the front. Triple Force, His Finest Hour, and Draupnir are all prominent-style horses who will contest the early positions behind Poet's Dawn, meaning the pace is real enough to stretch the field but unlikely to be suicidal on soft ground. The two genuine hold-up horses in the field — Cosmos Raj and Precious Spartan — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot realistically find their true rear position in a field of this size and style composition; the field holds more hold-up types than can slot neatly to the back, meaning those horses will race closer to the pace than ideal. This shape — a sole, uncontested leader setting a sustainable but honest Soft-ground gallop, tracked by a clutch of prominent types — firmly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, with pure hold-up finishing kicks less likely to land if the fractions are not truly testing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn is allowed to bowl along at a controlled pace on the soft and the prominent chasers cannot close the gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Poet's Dawn sets a sustainable fractions on soft ground with no rival prepared to harry him, and his recent form — three wins in his last five — suggests he is in excellent nick for a flat 1m2f staying test; at eleven years old he remains a model front-runner and Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form at T14 6/79.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Triple Force, His Finest Hour, or Draupnir track Poet's Dawn closely and overhaul him in the soft ground final furlong where his stamina is tested.
scenarios.body: The combination of soft ground and 1m2f can expose an ageing front-runner if even one prominent rival has the class to stay on past him; His Finest Hour has placed twice on soft and brings good each-way form over this trip, while Draupnir has winning experience on similar going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and a late finisher cuts through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Yermanthere is the most likely beneficiary here given a genuine hold-up style and two second-place finishes over the same trip on good, though his soft-ground record is mixed; Cosmos Raj has the profile but is racing out of its natural rearward position, limiting the likelihood of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays significantly slower than expected and stamina becomes the defining factor, catching out runners not proven in testing conditions.
scenarios.body: No Knee Never and Precious Spartan have some soft-ground experience but inconsistent form, and in a true stamina grind any of the midfield types that stay on relentlessly could pick up minor honours; this is the least likely shape given the pace data points toward a controlled rather than truly gruelling contest.

watchPoints.text: Poet's Dawn — if he is allowed to stride clear into the straight uncontested, he is significantly harder to peg back on this soft Ripon surface and his current form gives him every right to be involved at the finish.

His Finest Hour — watch how promptly Warren Fentiman positions him in the first two furlongs; if he settles just behind Triple Force in second or third, he has the soft-ground placing form to suggest a bold showing is possible.

Yermanthere — monitor whether Rhys Elliott can find a clear passage from midfield turning for home, as traffic congestion in a soft-ground handicap at Ripon's relatively tight circuit could cost this hold-up horse dearly if he gets boxed in.

Triple Force — a 66-day absence after four consecutive placed or winning efforts at 1m-1m2f means fitness may be the key variable; if he travels smoothly for the first mile he could be dangerous, but if he blows up late the layoff is the reason.

Cosmos Raj and Precious Spartan — both are true hold-up horses racing closer to the pace than ideal today; if the pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field they retain some each-way claims, but their positional compromise means they are less likely to produce the clean finishing kick their form at its best implies.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Walt
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has run twice on six furlongs in better ground, with two fifth-place finishes; the drop to five furlongs on soft is sharper and more testing, and Rowan Scott will need a good pace to aim at — 66 days off the track adds a layer of uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Classyfied
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has run twice at five furlongs on good ground without winning, finishing fourth and fifth; back eight days after her last run and handled by David Allan, she is a confirmed hold-up type who needs the field to come back to her on the soft.|

runners_data.name: American Psycho
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort at five furlongs on good ground and has genuine hold-up tendencies; pushed into the midfield map because the field has more hold-up types than can all sit at the rear naturally, so Pierre-Louis Jamin may find himself further forward than ideal, which dilutes the finish he can produce.|

runners_data.name: Catavega
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with an unknown style and going profile, representing the Michael & David Easterby yard who are 4/35 in the last 14 days; Billy Garritty takes the ride and this runner is a significant unknown quantity — any positive debut performance could make them dangerous.|

runners_data.name: Empress Princess
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly was a promising second on debut over five furlongs on good ground and Daniel Tudhope's booking is a strong positive; prominent style suits tracking the front-runner, and the step up to soft going is the only real query for a horse who looks the most tactically well-placed in this field.|

runners_data.name: Kumharas
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey runner with no public form and an unknown style — Oisin Orr is a capable pilot who will assess the situation from the gates; soft ground on debut is a challenge but the unknown factor cuts both ways in an open novice.|

runners_data.name: The Resdev Roman
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Michael & David Easterby who has finished seventh in both career starts on good ground; Joanna Mason will look to control from the front but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations — setting the pace on soft ground without winning form is a difficult brief and rivals are likely to have her measure.|

races.paceDynamic: The Resdev Roman is the confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice sprint, and on soft ground over five furlongs at Ripon she will set a measured, sustainable tempo from the gates — her two previous runs both produced finishing positions of seventh, so she is unlikely to dictate with authority, but she will nonetheless shape the race from the front. Empress Princess is the most credible prominent racer in behind, finishing second on her sole start on good ground, and Daniel Tudhope will be looking to track the pace and challenge from a position of comfort. Walt and Classyfied are both hold-up types on form who will be ridden from off the pace, and the soft ground at Ripon — which genuinely tests stamina even over five furlongs — will reward those who travel smoothly and pick up late rather than those who burn energy early. This race shape, with one moderate front-runner and a credible prominent type in Empress Princess pressing from second, favours a prominent-to-mid racer who can settle just off the speed and sustain their effort through the soft ground to the line.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Empress Princess Controls Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Princess tracks The Resdev Roman closely and takes it up inside the final furlong, her prominence and soft-ground form hold up.
scenarios.body: Tudhope slots her into second immediately and she accelerates past The Resdev Roman approaching the final furlong, with the soft ground ensuring the lead is held against closers. Her sole run — a five-furlong second on good ground — suggests she has raw ability that translates well to this trip and this race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely testing on the soft and the front two tie each other up, giving hold-up horses a clear late run.
scenarios.body: Walt or Classyfied, both capable of finishing from off the pace, would benefit if the early sections are gruelling enough to stop the prominent runners reaching the line strongly. Soft going at Ripon over five furlongs can produce a wall of tired horses in the straight, making the well-ridden hold-up finisher dangerous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Catavega or Kumharas — both lightly raced and unquantified — produce debut or near-debut performances that immediately outclass the field on ability.
scenarios.body: Unraced or lightly raced types with unknown styles can surprise in novice company if they arrive with strong homework, and soft ground is a leveller that can suit the naturally talented newcomer. Either horse could slot into a prominent or midfield position and simply prove best on the day if the form horses underperform.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Roman Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If The Resdev Roman, freed up in front on soft ground, sets a moderate enough gallop to conserve energy and hold on against tardy closers.
scenarios.body: Her two runs suggest she lacks finishing gears, but if the pace is deliberately managed and the field behind her is slow to organise, a soft-ground slog could play into her hands. Joanna Mason would need to dictate precisely and the hold-up horses would need to be caught flat-footed — an unlikely but non-zero scenario.

watchPoints.text: Empress Princess — Tudhope's positioning in the first furlong is critical; if she misses the break or is checked early, her entire race plan unravels and the scenario probabilities shift markedly toward the closers.

The Resdev Roman — watch whether she is allowed a soft lead or is hustled by Empress Princess from the off; a contested early pace on soft ground would increase stamina demands and raise the chance of hold-up horses Walt and Classyfied finishing strongly.

Catavega and Kumharas — both are unknown quantities with no public form; monitor market moves before the off, as significant support for either would imply strong gallops at home and could make the debutant scenario more credible.

Walt — 66 days off the track for David Loughnane's hold-up juvenile; watch early for any signs of ring-rustiness or reluctance to settle, as a freshness-induced forward move would take him entirely out of his natural hold-up role on soft ground.

races.name: 21 Engineer Regiment Sapper Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lexington Boom
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with improving form (2-2-1 last three, all on Good at 5f) and a current winning sequence, though how it handles the step to Soft going for the first time is the key unknown — Grant Tuer's yard is out of form at 0/12 over 14 days, adding a stable concern.|
runners_data.comment: Lexington Boom arrives in fine nick, winning last time out and filling the runner-up spot in two of his three subsequent starts, with experience over today's trip and a lively weight-to-rating profile adding further appeal.

runners_data.name: Roman Crystal
runners_data.note: Has won over 6f on Good but has shown consistent decline stepping back in trip (six runs, one win, multiple late finishes), and five recent runs all on Good ground suggest the Soft is uncharted territory; likely to fight for the lead without truly controlling it.|
runners_data.comment: Roman Crystal arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with 24 days between runs suggesting she comes here fresh and ready; the main risk is that her speed rating of 65 leaves her with something to find against the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' filly has won twice recently over 6f on Good, but her sim-going record on similar going reads 2/7 with zero wins and zero places, raising a genuine soft-ground flag; the switch down to 5f from her preferred 6f is also unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Lady Dublin won back-to-back races three and two starts back, and with experience over today's trip and our rating putting her top of these rivals, she looks the one to beat; the worry is that disappointing eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Star People
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner (headgear: b) in sharp form with three consecutive placed runs, Jason Hart in the saddle for an in-form Quinn yard (4/17 T14), and a recent run over 5f on Soft-adjacent ground at Sandown suggests she won't be caught cold by conditions — the most likely pace-setter to secure the lead cleanly.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in fine nick, Star People brings strong claims here: second last time out and again three starts back, with experience over today's trip and a quick 12-day turnaround suggesting he's in good order. The main risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: May Bee In Profit
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prominent type holds the most relevant form line in the race — a second over 5f on Soft — giving her a clear going advantage over most rivals; David Allan partnerships with Easterby runners have been productive (6/79 T14) and she's in sharp order off 12 days.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, May Bee In Profit has shown some ability — a winner and placed efforts feature in recent starts — but a sixth and an unplaced run since make her hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's trip and returns fit enough at 12 days.

runners_data.name: Inca Warrior
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's two-year-old has only two runs to its name (both fourths on Good at 5f), returns after a 45-day absence with a 0/17 trainer 14-day strike rate, and while a natural prominent type, is shown toward the rear by field redistribution — its ability to deliver a meaningful late challenge from an unnatural position is genuinely questionable.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Inca Warrior faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip before and a 45-day break may have freshened him from stall one at 128 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Star People, Lexington Boom, and Roman Crystal are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field, guaranteeing an aggressive battle for the lead from the off over Ripon's straight five furlongs on Soft ground. The three pace-setters will push one another into an unsustainable gallop, meaning the race will be run at a strong tempo from start to finish with no respite — Soft ground will amplify the energy cost dramatically, turning this into a genuine stamina examination despite the sprint trip. Lady Dublin and May Bee In Profit, both prominent types comfortable racing just off the pace, are ideally placed to exploit a pace meltdown in the final furlong, tracking the combusting leaders before picking up the pieces. The field holds more front-running or prominent types than can all command early position, and of the three nominal pace-setters, Star People (class, recent form, Jason Hart) and Lexington Boom (stronger recent form figures) are most likely to actually secure the rail and dictate early, with Roman Crystal likely pressuring from alongside rather than leading cleanly — this race shape emphatically favours prominent-to-tracking horses with proven stamina and soft-ground credentials.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out inside the final two furlongs, handing the race to the prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: The brutal early pace on Soft ground will drain the leaders, leaving Lady Dublin and May Bee In Profit — both comfortable settling just behind the speed — to coast past the tying front-runners in the closing stages. Lady Dublin's two recent wins and May Bee In Profit's soft-ground placed run (2nd/5f/SOF) make both profiles perfectly suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Star People or Lexington Boom breaks sharply enough to establish a clear lead and the others cannot sustain contact on the Soft ground.
scenarios.body: A single confirmed front-runner who gets away cleanly and controls the pace without being pressed could find the Soft ground less punishing than rivals who expend energy fighting for position early. Star People has proven fitness (12 days since last run, recent placed form) and Jason Hart's course savvy, while Lexington Boom's winning form on Good gives it claims if it handles the Soft and finds a clear route.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Steady
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong but not catastrophic, rewarding a horse that stays prominent without burning out in the scramble.
scenarios.body: May Bee In Profit's soft-ground placing and David Allan's tactical experience could allow it to sit just off the blistering pace and sustain its run better than leaders who have fought for position. Lady Dublin similarly carries a strong recent record and could hold enough pace to dominate if the fractions are fast but not lethal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that even the prominent types are compromised, leaving a deep closer to mop up in the final strides.
scenarios.body: Inca Warrior is shown at the rear by redistribution — in reality a naturally prominent horse running out of role, meaning this scenario depends on a type not truly suited to late-closing tactics, which significantly discounts it. Even in a maximum pace meltdown, Inca Warrior's limited form (two fourths, 45 days off) gives little confidence it can execute a genuine late run.

watchPoints.text: Star People, Lexington Boom, and Roman Crystal — three confirmed front-runners in six cannot all lead; watch the first two furlongs for early crowding, bumping, or one runner being checked and losing momentum completely.

Lady Dublin's soft-ground record (sim-going: 2/7, 0 wins, 0 places) is a red flag that could see the OR 75 top-weight underperform despite strong recent form — watch whether she handles the ground in early strides or appears to be struggling through it.

May Bee In Profit has the stand-out relevant form (2nd/5f/Soft) in the field — if she obtains a clean position just off the pace in the first furlong, she becomes a significant danger to all in the final stages when the leaders tie up.

Inca Warrior — 45 days off, trainer out of form (0/17 T14), and being asked to race in an unnatural hold-up position; watch whether it settles at the rear under Rowan Scott or gets shuffled back involuntarily and is never competitive.

The Soft ground on a straight five furlongs at Ripon historically favours horses that can relax and sustain pace over those who sprint hard early — monitor which runners are visibly labouring through the ground in the first half of the race as a guide to the finish order.

races.name: Ripon Yorkshire's Garden Racecourse Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Ruth Carr and James Sullivan, best form on good ground (0 wins, 0 places from 15 soft-equivalent runs), but has won over 5f on good — stepping up to 6f and facing softer conditions is a concern, though prominent style suits the predicted race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Reigning Profit has finished eighth last time out and was unplaced two starts back, and with our rating placing him eighth of ten runners he is hard to fancy at the weights; experience over today's trip and going is a slim but genuine foothold.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has placed twice in similar going conditions and is proven at 6f, with Tom Eaves booked; a prominent runner with the best similar-going record of the pace-tracking pair, and the drop from good-ground form to soft is moderate rather than catastrophic.
runners_data.comment: Arduis Invicta showed plenty when finishing second three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going is a genuine asset at 136 lb from stall nine; the concern is she has been winless in recent starts, with a couple of unplaced efforts among her recent runs to account for.

runners_data.name: Charlie Mason
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll yard is in cracking form (4/41 over 14 days) and the horse has won on soft at 6f — however, his natural hold-up style means he is genuinely placed further up the field here than he'd like, and Callum Rodriguez will need to be creative to find a run if forced to race closer than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Charlie Mason won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, so conditions pose no obvious concern; at 134 lb from stall 4, the weight burden is the key question after three unplaced efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner has strong placed form at 6f on good ground and is one of the most consistent horses in the field, but has only run twice on soft equivalent going without a win or place — quick turnaround (4 days) is also worth flagging though O'Meara regularly operates this way with Tudhope aboard.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and twice more in recent starts, Yes I'm Mali arrives just four days on from that effort carrying 141 lb from stall 10, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; yet to win in his last six starts, but his rating of 88 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Top Juggler
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner: Seb Spencer's four-year-old has won at 6f on good ground and placed on soft over 5f, making him the key pace influence; his tagged STYLE_FIT score reflects that dictating in this field is slightly above his natural grade, but no rival is set to seriously challenge him for the lead.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and was second three starts back, but a seventh last time out clouds the picture; has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs suggests he returns fresh enough, though 139 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Kind Touch
runners_data.note: Fahey three-year-old who has placed on soft ground over 6f and won at 5f — longest absence of any runner here at 52 days, which with a yard firing at 6/44 is a mild concern; genuine hold-up type who needs things to go right late, but the going suits.

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby filly wearing headgear (hg:t), with consistent midfield-to-rear finishes at 6f on good ground and modest placed form on soft — Easterby sends out plenty (6/79 in 14 days) but this filly's form figures don't inspire, and she'll need the pace to collapse to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Anaisa has nonetheless shown consistent midfield form with a pair of fourths and a fifth in that spell, and she has experience over today's distance and going; at 133 lb from stall seven, there is plenty to do, but a 17-day turnaround keeps her fresh.

runners_data.name: Secret Guest
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's six-year-old has a sparse recent record (1/4 over 14 days) and a poor recent form string; he's a true hold-up horse pushed forward on the map due to redistribution, meaning he will not settle where he travels best — his chance depends on a scenario that is unlikely to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Secret Guest nevertheless rates a shade above his official mark on our figures and has run over today's trip and going before; the fourth last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, though his overall recent record makes it hard to fancy him strongly from stall three carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's seven-year-old has been an extraordinary place-getter on good ground (four consecutive second-place finishes) but was tenth on soft over 6f last time — he's a natural closer who is genuinely racing out of position in this race shape, and the going switch is a notable concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts despite a run of three consecutive runner-up finishes a couple of starts back, Another Investment has since slipped to sixth and ranks ninth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Easterby's second runner wears a hood (hg:b) and has placed twice on soft at 5f but has never won under these conditions; a true hold-up type who is mapped closer than ideal, with a low OR and a form string that shows more placing on good ground than soft.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Spirit Of Applause faces a stiff task as the bottom-ranked runner on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh ten-day break carrying 129 lb from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Top Juggler is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead in this 10-runner field, he is set to bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo on soft ground at Ripon's straight six. Reigning Profit and Arduis Invicta will push forward from their prominent styles and likely track Top Juggler through the early stages, but neither has the profile or the mandate to seriously press him for supremacy. The bulk of the field — Charlie Mason, Yes I'm Mali, Kind Touch, Anaisa, Secret Guest, Another Investment and Spirit Of Applause — are genuine hold-up or midfield types, several of whom are redistributed because the field is back-heavy and cannot all settle where they would naturally wish; the hold-up horses most likely to genuinely get a rear position are Yes I'm Mali, Kind Touch and Anaisa, while Charlie Mason, Secret Guest, Another Investment and Spirit Of Applause are true closers who will be forced wider or closer to the pace than ideal. On soft ground over six furlongs at Ripon, a single uncontested front-runner dictating a measured gallop strongly favours those tracking just off the pace in the prominent-to-midfield berths, as the closer cluster will face traffic and a slower-than-expected tempo that blunts their finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Top Juggler secures the lead unchallenged and sets a soft-ground rhythm that suits those in his slipstream.
scenarios.body: Top Juggler rolls along at an uncontested tempo, and the prominent duo of Reigning Profit and Arduis Invicta are ideally placed to pounce in the final two furlongs as the pace softens late on soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Get Lucky Gap
scenarios.trigger: If Top Juggler sets a genuinely strong pace that strings the field out and creates a gap for closers to exploit late.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop from Top Juggler on soft ground causes the prominent horses to pay for their early effort, leaving the genuine hold-up horses such as Yes I'm Mali and Kind Touch with daylight to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going and lack of pressure allow Top Juggler to conserve energy and simply outstay rivals from the front.
scenarios.body: Soft ground rewards a relaxed, energy-efficient gallop, and a horse who has led from the front and won over this course-and-distance profile can simply refuse to be caught as rivals burn fuel chasing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide and the hold-up horses mapped to midfield — Charlie Mason, Secret Guest, Another Investment — somehow find clear passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because all three are tagged as redistributed and will not be racing in their natural position; if the pace collapses unusually quickly and they find a run, their soft-ground form gives a slim chance.

watchPoints.text: Top Juggler controls every other runner's race — if he gets loose on the front end unchallenged, he is a significant threat to simply stay on and not be caught on this soft ground.

Another Investment's soft-ground record (10th on his only soft 6f run) is a sharp contrast to his good-ground placing sequence — watch for him to underperform his market position if punters back him on the back of those placed efforts.

Yes I'm Mali runs just four days after his last outing — David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope operate quick turnarounds routinely, but watch the market to see if this is a confident or precautionary runner.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Charlie Mason, Secret Guest, Another Investment, Spirit Of Applause — means the middle of the field may be congested in the straight, creating a traffic-risk that benefits horses with the clearest passage (Top Juggler, Arduis Invicta, Reigning Profit).

Kind Touch's 52-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — Fahey's yard is active but watch the market as a first-time spin back from a break on soft ground over 6f for a three-year-old carries a fitness question that form alone cannot resolve.

races.name: Ripon Yorkshire's Garden Racecourse Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Here Forever
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won at 6f on Good recently (1/6f/GOO) but now faces Soft for the first time at this distance and must fight Goyard for the lead; David & Nicola Barron trainer form is 0/7 in the last 14 days which is a cold flag, and at 57 days since last run freshness is uncertain.|
runners_data.comment: Here Forever has managed one win in his last five starts and, ranked ninth of ten on our figures, is hard to fancy at these weights, though he has run over today's trip before and the run fifty-seven days ago leaves room for improvement.

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: Has been in fine recent form with multiple placed efforts including two wins and a second over 6-7f on Good; Grant Tuer's runner arrives on just 10 days' rest, suits a prominent position, and similar-going form (2/15, 0W2P) suggests soft conditions are a question mark.|
runners_data.comment: Farandaway has winning form in recent starts and returns on a quick turnaround just ten days after his last run, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour, but ranked eighth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff ask at 134 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Wobwobwob
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who arrives on 11 days' rest with a tongue-tie and a soft-ground record that reads 0W3P from 10 similar-going runs; the note on fading in the finish is significant over 6f on Soft, and at age 8 his chance depends entirely on a strong pace collapsing the field late enough.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with a pair of ninths and two unplaced efforts among them, Wobwobwob makes little appeal from stall six carrying 133 lb, and our rating of 72 ranks him last of ten; experience over today's trip and going, plus a sharp 11-day turnaround, offer scant consolation.

runners_data.name: Almarada Prince
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan partners this five-year-old who has been placed consistently at this trip (3/6f/GOO, 2/6f/GOO) and holds a hold-up style well suited to a hot-pace scenario; soft-going record is modest (0W0P from 2 runs) but his recent form trajectory is encouraging and 39 days off should leave him fresh.|
runners_data.comment: Almarada Prince shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, and third three starts back underlines his consistency at this level; rated 84 by us, he carries 140 lb from stall one, and the chief concern is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Venture Capital
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing five-year-old who has struggled to translate his style into form, with form figures of 89087 in recent outings and 0W1P from two similar-going runs; the hood is a factor and Kevin Ryan's 3/34 in 14 days suggests no notable hot spell from the yard.|
runners_data.comment: Venture Capital returns after 31 days with experience over today's trip and going in his favour, and our rating of 87 marks him as the one to beat in a field of ten, though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find improvement to justify that standing.

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a tongue-tie who recorded a win on Soft (1W from 2 soft-going runs) and is the more seasoned of the two pace-setters; David O'Meara's operation is 3/40 in the last 14 days, and Goyard must decide immediately whether to press Here Forever or cede — that tactical call from Tudhope shapes the race.|
runners_data.comment: Goyard arrives on the back of a fifth last time out and has been winless in his last five starts, though a third four starts back offers a flicker of encouragement; he has distance and going experience and returns after a 21-day break carrying 137 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Prominent type in the care of Tim Easterby (6/79 in 14 days), wearing a hood, who has recent experience at this trip including a second at 6f on Good; soft-going record is blank (0W0P) and his form figures of 320055 suggest he is running into a purple patch only slowly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mister Sox does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and steps back up having shaped with a little more promise when second and third in earlier efforts, though back-to-back fifths most recently are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old hold-up runner who found 2/6f/GOO recently and retains ability when conditions set up a strong pace; 39 days off and a mixed soft-ground record (0W0P from 2 runs) temper confidence, but Ben Haslam's placing of him here suggests he is ready to run well.|
runners_data.comment: Fortamour shaped with promise when second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead from stall seven carrying 132 lb; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: First Folio
runners_data.note: Has genuine hold-up instincts and his best form comes when racing from the rear, but this competitive 6f on Soft with prominent horses stacked ahead of him means he is unlikely to secure his natural position; the visor is fitted and recent 6f form shows consistency (4/6f/GOO, 6/6f/GOO) but the style mismatch in this race shape limits his prospects.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, First Folio nevertheless catches the eye with a rating of 82 that puts him well clear of his official mark, and he has run over today's distance and going before; the worry is that his recent record offers little encouragement of a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: Four-year-old filly for Philip Kirby (2/8 in 14 days) whose best efforts (3/6f/GOO, 3/7f/GOO) have come from a hold-up role, but in this field she is unlikely to find real daylight at the rear to make her run; her true finishing kick is compromised by the number of hold-up types ahead of her, and soft-going form (0W0P from 4 runs) adds a further concern.|
runners_data.comment: Educating Rita has shown she can hit the frame, with thirds two and five starts back, but has otherwise struggled for consistency and remains yet to win in her last five starts; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 17 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Here Forever and Goyard are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 6f on Soft ground at Ripon, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead for either. That friction between two honest pace-setters across sticky ground is likely to set a strong tempo that tests stamina reserves in the final furlong, making the race genuinely attritional. Farandaway, Venture Capital, and Mister Sox add prominent energy behind them, meaning there will be no vacuum in the early-mid section — the field will be strung out and racing hard from the gun. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and late-running profiles who can conserve energy in the first half and pick up those who have emptied, with Almarada Prince and Fortamour the natural beneficiaries of a strong pace meltdown. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race map can place naturally — First Folio and Educating Rita are genuine rear-runners who are mapped to midfield positions they are unlikely to hold given how aggressively the pace section will be contested, and both should be discounted in shapes that require them to race from a true hold-up position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Here Forever and Goyard fight a genuine duel up front on Soft ground and the prominent section is also under pressure, creating a truly strong gallop that sets up a final-furlong collapse.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners drain each other and the prominent horses tracking them, leaving the race wide open for those holding energy deepest into the race; Almarada Prince and Fortamour are ideally placed to pick up the pieces having been sheltered from the early friction.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Here Forever or Goyard secures an uncontested lead after the rival capitulates early, stealing a breather and controlling the tempo on Soft ground to a degree that makes them hard to catch.
scenarios.body: One pacesetter breaks clear and is allowed to bowl along at a controlled rate, and the sticky surface means chasers never quite get to them in time; Here Forever's recent win at 6f on Good (form: 1/6f/GOO) and Goyard's win on Soft suggest both are capable of front-running effectiveness in these conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Track Bias
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses after the initial duel and a prominent horse sitting just behind the leaders tracks up into a perfect position without having burned energy in the opening duel.
scenarios.body: Farandaway, who has been running prominently to good effect with recent placed efforts, could slot behind the leaders and benefit as the front-runners weaken without being dragged into their battle; Mister Sox has course experience and could profile similarly if he settles just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Denied Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves moderate despite two nominal front-runners — perhaps one defers early — leaving genuine hold-up horses with no pace to close into.
scenarios.body: True hold-up operators First Folio and Educating Rita are already racing out of their natural rear-of-field positions, reducing the likelihood they can execute their finishing style effectively; even if late ground opens up, those mapped rearward are unlikely to be in the right spot to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Here Forever and Goyard go head-to-head for the lead from stall — watch which horse blinks first in the opening furlong, as the one forced to settle second may fade significantly on the Soft ground having still burned early energy.|

Almarada Prince's jockey David Nolan must find cover quickly behind the duel without getting caught in traffic — if he is squeezed or forced wide early on this flat 6f, his hold-up advantage evaporates.|
Wobwobwob is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, and at age 8 on Soft over 6f his chance is almost entirely pace-dependent — if the gallop is even slightly moderate, he will not get home.|

Farandaway arrives on just 10 days' rest following a busy campaign, and while his recent form is solid, watch whether Oliver Stammers can keep him off the early pace pressure generated by the two front-runners — any overcooking early will cost him late.|

First Folio and Educating Rita are unlikely to race from their natural deep hold-up positions given the field shape — if either is seen pushing forward to gain ground in the early-mid section, treat it as a significant tactic shift worth noting for the run-in.|

races.name: attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Tim Easterby, David Allan takes the ride; recent form all on good ground at Ascot (sim-going record 3/15 with no wins) flags a soft-ground question mark despite course form, and at age 11 relying on habit and guts rather than raw ability — the key pace-setter but vulnerable when the ground tests stamina.
runners_data.comment: Garden Oasis has been consistently knocking at the door, finishing third, third, and second in his last three starts, and our rating of 80 puts him among the very best in this field; the risk is that he remains winless and may again find one too good.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing four-year-old for David O'Meara, with Daniel Tudhope booked — form reads as consistent without winning but has a clear profile of running just off the pace which suits this race shape exactly; all recent form on good ground, soft is an unknown, but the style fit here is strong.
runners_data.comment: Donna Nook shaped with promise when third last time out and is a winner in her last six starts, with experience over today's trip and a fitness edge at just 18 days since her latest run; her rating of 81 marks her as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Catton Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won on soft last time (7f) and has two placed efforts on soft ground, giving her the best soft-ground profile in the field; Joanna Mason continues the partnership, and stepping back up to a mile from seven furlongs where she landed a win should suit her staying style.
runners_data.comment: Catton Lady arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here, and she carries 139 lb from stall nine as the main threat to her chances.

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who won on good at eight furlongs but has only one run on a similar-going surface in this field — her form over this exact trip and at Ripon is untested on soft, but Kevin Stott is a strong booking and she is one of the few authentic closers in the race.
runners_data.comment: Kiss Me My Love has placed third last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, but an unplaced effort three starts back tempers confidence; carrying 137 lb from stall 3, she holds claims without being certain to improve on a mixed recent profile.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with soft-ground placed form (2nd over 10f, 5th over 10f on soft) and a win at nine furlongs on good; OR=64 and a mile on soft may be at the limit of her stamina, but Grant Tuer's runner has a better soft-ground record than most rivals and Oliver Stammers is competent at this level.
runners_data.comment: Bellasio showed ability when winning two starts back, but his latest run was unplaced and, ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, he faces a stiff task at 134 lb, though he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Annie
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old whose entire recent form comes on good ground; her only soft run produced a modest effort (1/12 in similar going), and a 3lb claimer Jack Nicholls takes over — headgear of hood likely helps with focus but the going is a genuine concern for this filly.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Annie showed plenty when a second two starts back, but a seventh last time out clouds her chance here; she has run over today's trip and a 34-day break leaves fitness mildly in question, though she carries 133 lb from stall 13 with a rating edge over her mark.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Joy
runners_data.note: 57-day absence is the headline concern; natural back-marker pushed into midfield mapping because the rear of the field is overcrowded with hold-up types, meaning she is unlikely to get the covering ground she needs. Soft ground (1/6 sim-going) has not been kind, and her recent form string includes a 9th on soft.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Hopeful Joy has been out of the frame in three of her four most recent outings, and 57 days off the track adds a fitness query; experience over today's trip is about the best that can be said for her.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with three placed efforts on soft (2nd twice), giving him a fair soft-ground profile for the Easterby yard; natural hold-up style but has raced prominently enough in places, and the mile on soft should test his stamina rather than expose it — Billy Garritty's local knowledge an asset.
runners_data.comment: Milford Grange has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 74 puts him ahead of his official mark — a solid case that he retains untapped ability, though he has been winless in his last six starts and must bounce back from a fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Paroda Diva
runners_data.note: Won on soft at eight furlongs (1/8f/SOF) and placed on soft — the soft-ground form is the most current of any horse in the race; in reality a hold-up or prominent type by preference, having to race out of that natural position given the congestion at the back, which tempers confidence despite the going credentials.
runners_data.comment: Paroda Diva won three starts back but was sixth last time out, leaving her form difficult to assess heading here; she has run over today's trip and returns after 22 days, though her speed rating of 64 may leave her with ground to make up from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Consistent non-winner over recent starts with a form string showing 10th, 4th, 10th, 11th — the direction of travel is flat; true nature is a hold-up or prominent horse by headgear note (p), repositioned to midfield on the map due to field congestion, and David Nolan cannot manufacture talent that isn't there on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Zermatt Star does at least return after a 26-day break with experience over today's trip in her favour, though a fourth two starts back represents her best recent effort and she faces a stiff task from draw seven carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: G'Emmethegreenlite
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up from six and seven furlongs to a mile on soft — the trip extension is the key question mark; tailed hood (t) may aid concentration, but recent form includes a 9th on soft and an 11th, and this horse has been mapped away from its natural back position due to the sheer number of hold-up types in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures, G'Emmethegreenlite faces a stiff ask here; a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround of 13 days.

runners_data.name: Gunalt Wavelength
runners_data.note: Won twice at seven furlongs on good ground earlier in the season and was placed twice, but soft-ground form (6/14 in similar going, no wins) and a 38-day break give pause; a natural hold-up type moved forward on the map by necessity rather than by style, and Shay Farmer's 5lb claim needs to offset inexperience at this level.
runners_data.comment: Gunalt Wavelength won two of her last five starts, with a fourth and sixth in more recent outings suggesting she may need things to fall right, though she has experience over today's trip and going, and 38 days between runs keeps fitness under scrutiny.

runners_data.name: Penny Ghent
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner, wears a hood (b) and has won twice at eight furlongs in recent starts; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helps offset a moderate OR of 58, and Simon Whitaker's runner goes from 34 days off — soft-ground record is poor (3/15, no wins), which raises the question of whether she can maintain her natural front-running style when the ground gets into her.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Penny Ghent faces a stiff ask here, though she does arrive with two wins in her last six starts and has run over today's trip and going before, offering some small crumbs of comfort from stall two off 34 days.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent are the two confirmed front-runners in this 13-runner handicap over a mile on soft ground at Ripon, and with both likely to stride forward from the off, an honest, contested gallop is the expected tempo rather than any false economy. That sustained pace over a mile on testing ground will put a premium on stamina and the ability to stay close enough to the action without burning too much fuel — a profile that suits horses racing prominently or from a close-tracking midfield position. The field carries considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Zermatt Star, Paroda Diva, G'Emmethegreenlite, Hopeful Joy, and Gunalt Wavelength are genuine back-markers by nature but have been pushed into midfield on the map because the true rear is overcrowded, meaning several will race out of their preferred position. The tactical verdict is clear: with two genuine front-runners setting a genuine gallop on soft ground, prominent racers and close-tracking types who can conserve energy early and travel into the race are best placed, while true hold-up horses face a compromised scenario as they are unlikely to secure their natural ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent fight for the lead and set a true end-to-end gallop on soft ground, burning out the principals.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will string the field out and exhaust the front two, handing the race to a prominent or close-tracking type who travels within themselves before picking up in the home straight; soft ground rewards the stamina of horses who race efficiently just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners, most likely Garden Oasis, gets a softer lead and is allowed to control the tempo from a comfortable position.
scenarios.body: An unchallenged front-runner on soft ground at Ripon can steal a march and prove difficult to reel in if the pace is allowed to become honest but not brutal; Garden Oasis's course form and jockey David Allan's experience at this track make this a realistic shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lates
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go hard enough to collapse on themselves and leave room for a late finisher to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Catton Lady and Kiss Me My Love both hold soft-ground form and are genuine hold-up types who could benefit if the race falls apart up front; however, most horses mapped to the rear are redistributed types who are unlikely to truly sit last, limiting the depth of the closing surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind-Through
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows everything to a stamina test and midfield horses with proven soft-ground credentials grind past a weakening leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Bellasio showed a win at nine furlongs on good ground and placed on soft, while Milford Grange has multiple placed efforts on soft and stays the mile well; neither needs to be close early but both have the cruising speed to pick through a strung-out field if the race becomes a war of attrition.

watchPoints.text: Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent may clash for the lead immediately — watch for either jockey to soften the tempo rather than fight, which would transform this from a true-run gallop into a falsely-paced affair that hands an advantage to whichever front-runner settles better.

Catton Lady's soft-ground winning form is the standout going-related credential in the field — watch her position from the half-mile pole, as she is likely to make ground late and could be the dominant closer if the pace scenario unfolds as expected.

Several redistributed hold-up types (Zermatt Star, G'Emmethegreenlite, Hopeful Joy, Gunalt Wavelength) will be competing for the same midfield ground and could block each other's runs in the straight on soft going — scrimmaging in the pack is a real risk.

Penny Ghent's soft-ground record (0 wins, 3 places from 15 attempts on similar going) raises a serious doubt about her ability to maintain front-running momentum as the race progresses — watch for her to drop away from two furlongs out, leaving Garden Oasis as the sole pace-maker.

Milford Grange's three placed efforts on soft ground make him a quiet improver to track — if Easterby's stable is in form (4/35 in 14 days) and the mile on soft brings out his best, he could emerge from midfield late without attracting much market attention.

races.name: Wakeman Stayers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose recent form has been entirely on Good ground at distances up to 17f; the step to 2m on soft is unexplored territory in the sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs on similar), making this a notable ground/trip combination query for Micky Hammond's 4-year-old.|
runners_data.comment: Twilight Safari arrives here on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, and a third three starts back underlines his consistency in recent outings; yet to win in his last five starts, he rates our top pick on a mark of 77 and has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Zimmerman
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7-year-old brings a solid profile at 16-17f but all five recent runs have come on Good or Good-to-Firm; David Allan rides and the 85-day absence is a minor concern, though Easterby's 6/79 14-day strike rate suggests horses leave the yard ready.|
runners_data.comment: Zimmerman has shown consistent improvement in recent starts, placing second and third earlier in the campaign before a sixth last time out, and has experience over today's distance and going; the main concern is 85 days off the track, though he looks a strong threat at the weights carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Bollin Neil
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shape anchor; 223 days off is a significant fitness query for a 10-year-old but Tim Easterby fits tongue-tie and he has winning and placed form on soft, giving him a clear tactical edge if fitness holds.|
runners_data.comment: Bollin Neil brings back-to-back wins into this, scoring two starts and three starts back respectively, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is a 223-day absence which leaves his current fitness very much the question.

runners_data.name: Dereham
runners_data.note: John Berry's 10-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by nature — pushed forward on the pace map only because the field's rear is saturated with closers — so his chance is contingent on an unusually honest pace that he can close into; one soft-going run in recent history (unknown finishing position) limits confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and again five starts back, Dereham returns in good order after 24 days and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Femme Fatale
runners_data.note: James Tate's 3-year-old is the only authentic prominent runner behind Bollin Neil, giving Daniel Tudhope a natural position tracking the leader; won over 2m on Standard and placed at 2m on Soft, so the trip and surface combination hold no fears, and the tongue-tie flags a horse that needs to race professionally.|

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Won last time at Chelmsford over 2m on Standard and arrives freshest of the closers at 15 days; a natural hold-up type placed into midfield on the map because of the crowded rear, so the style-fit caveat applies — Ben Case's 7-year-old needs things to go right positionally to reproduce that winning run.|
runners_data.comment: Regally Blonde is ranked bottom of six on our figures and her recent form is patchy, with just one win in her last six starts, though that victory came last time out and she returns on a fresh 15-day break with distance and going experience in her favour.

runners_data.name: Si White
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3-year-old is a genuine hold-up specialist by record, but crowding at the back means Dylan Hogan may be forced wider or closer than ideal; the visor is fitted for the first time and all five recent runs have been on Standard, making soft ground a notable unknown despite Prescott's typically thorough preparation.|
runners_data.comment: Si White scrambles home a winner three starts back but has finished fifth and third since, and our rating of 62 ranks him fifth of six here, making him hard to fancy at these weights; he has run over today's trip and returns after 24 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Bollin Neil is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over two miles on soft ground at Ripon. At a distance where energy conservation is paramount and the soft going will amplify the cost of chasing, a horse allowed to control his own fractions from the front is in a privileged tactical position — particularly a 10-year-old whose entire career profile is built around front-running. The chasing pack will be forced to make a decision early: commit to tracking Bollin Neil and risk doing too much work in the conditions, or sit off and hope to close a potentially decisive gap in the straight. This shape firmly favours a confirmed hold-up or prominent horse with genuine soft-ground stamina who can reel in a relaxed front-runner late — but note that Si White, Dereham, and Regally Blonde are all true hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning this field's rear end is genuinely congested with closers and Femme Fatale, as the only authentic prominent runner, is most likely to actually secure a position close to Bollin Neil in the early stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bollin Neil Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bollin Neil is allowed to stride clear at his own pace and the soft ground slows the closers enough to prevent a meaningful challenge.
scenarios.body: Bollin Neil settles into a relaxed rhythm on the front end, and two miles of soft ground at Ripon saps the finishing energy of those held up in rear; by the time the closers ask questions in the straight, the deficit is too great to bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Reels Him In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bollin Neil's 223-day absence tells in the final quarter-mile and a well-placed hold-up runner sustains a run through soft ground.
scenarios.body: A chaser who has settled beautifully in the mid-to-rear pack gets a clear run entering the straight and gradually picks off Bollin Neil, whose fitness from a long layoff may see him flatten out inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Femme Fatale Tracks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Femme Fatale uses her prominent style to sit just off Bollin Neil, conserves energy through the race, and finds more than the front-runner in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Having won over 2m on Standard going at Chelmsford and placed recently, the 3-year-old Femme Fatale times her challenge to strike as Bollin Neil ties up, her youth and relative freshness proving decisive in the ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and the redistributed hold-up horses (Si White, Regally Blonde, Dereham) find themselves racing out of their natural pattern, scrambling the finish.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their preferred position and unable to dictate their own rhythm, the redistributed closers contribute to a muddled finish; a horse with class at the top of the weights benefits from the resulting positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Bollin Neil's 223-day absence is the single biggest variable in the race — if he blows up physically in the soft ground before the straight, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the hold-up horses inherit a very different race shape than expected.

Femme Fatale is the only natural tracker in the field; if Daniel Tudhope elects to sit further back than usual to conserve energy, he removes her key tactical advantage and the race becomes a test of pure stamina between Bollin Neil and the closers.

Si White, Dereham, and Regally Blonde are all genuine hold-up types compressed into a tight pocket at the rear — watch for traffic problems in the straight at Ripon, where the run-in is relatively short and a clear passage is not guaranteed for all three.

The soft going is consistent across all seven Ripon races today, with no variance in the report; there is no drying or bias angle to exploit, and stamina will be the primary differentiator at 2m in these conditions.
